author: Horsfield, 1821
habitat: 전나무·잣나무·소나무·참나무·밤나무 등이 섞여 자라는 침엽수·활엽수 혼효림
summary: 예전에는 경기도에 살았으나 지금은 관찰되지 않는 새이다. 전나무·잣나무·소나무·참나무·밤나무 등 침엽수와 활엽수가 섞여 자라는 숲에 살며, 주로 이른 아침과 저녁에 움직이지만 흐리거나 비가 오는 날에는 낮에도 활동한다. 나무줄기를 나선을 그리며 타고 올라 이웃 나무로 건너가고, 나무껍질을 벗기고 구멍을 파서 큰 딱정벌레 애벌레를 꺼내 먹는다. 참나무·전나무·소나무 등의 나무 구멍을 쓰거나 직접 구멍을 파서 둥지로 삼고, 5~6월에 흰 알 2~5개를 낳아 암수가 번갈아 품는다.

art.subject: White-bellied Woodpecker (Dryocopus javensis richardsi, the Korean race), adult male: deep red forehead, crown and pointed nape crest; a dark red malar stripe from the base of the bill; the rest of the head, the neck, throat and upper breast black; back, wings and tail black; lower back, rump and uppertail coverts white; lower breast and belly white, sharply divided from the black upper breast. Long, chisel-tipped black bill; pale yellowish iris; blackish-grey legs.
art.pose: spiralling up a large trunk, prising off bark to dig out beetle larvae
art.scene: Korean mixed forest of firs, Korean pines, pines, oaks and chestnut trees at dawn; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging upright to a trunk: deep red forehead, crown and crest, dark red malar stripe, pale yellowish eye, black head sides, neck and upper breast, white lower breast and belly, black wings and tail, long black bill, blackish-grey legs
adult female, head detail: forehead, crown and crest all black without red, and the malar area black with no red stripe
adult, back view on a trunk: white lower back, rump and uppertail coverts contrasting with the black mantle, wings and stiff black tail
art.build: Very large woodpecker, 46cm, about the size of a crow and slightly larger than the Black Woodpecker; long-necked and slim-bodied, with a pointed crest at the back of the head. Bill long, straight and chisel-tipped, about as long as the head. Legs short, blackish grey, with strong toes, two forward and two back, gripping the trunk. Tail black, stiff and wedge-shaped, pressed against the trunk as a prop. In flight the white rump and white belly contrast with the black upperparts.
avoid: Do not paint it all black like the Black Woodpecker (Dryocopus martius); the white rump and white belly are essential.
Do not paint white on the throat, face or upper breast; the white begins below the black upper breast.
Do not add barring or spotting to the black parts of the plumage.
Do not give the female any red on the head.
